head: Nurses with
no managers.
slides.sub: How Buurtzorg rebuilt Dutch home care around small teams.

image.label: A nurse cycling through a Dutch neighborhood
image.brief: 네덜란드 주택가를 자전거로 달리는 방문 간호사. 인물은 실루엣 위주.

head: Care by the
stopwatch.
body: By the 2000s, Dutch home care had been reorganized for efficiency. Tasks were timed and split up, so one client might see many different carers in a week.

image.label: A stopwatch on a care schedule

head: A nurse leaves
the system.
body: In 2006, Jos de Blok, a nurse who had also worked as a manager in home care, started Buurtzorg, Dutch for "neighborhood care", with a small team.

image.label: A nurse at a kitchen table with an elderly client
image.brief: 부엌 식탁에서 노인 환자와 이야기하는 간호사.

head: You are growing fast.
How do you organize?
body: New teams are forming every month. Most care companies would hire managers now.

options.text: Add managers to coordinate the growing teams
options.feedback: The usual answer. It adds cost and distance from clients. Keep swiping.

options.text: Keep small self-run teams, with coaches instead of bosses
options.feedback: This is what Buurtzorg did. Keep swiping.
Fast, but harder to keep one way of working. Keep swiping.

image.label: A team of nurses around a table planning
image.brief: 테이블에 둘러앉아 일정을 짜는 간호사 팀.

head: Teams of
up to 12.
body: Each neighborhood team plans its own work, hires its own colleagues and decides how to care for each client.
A small back office handles pay and billing. Regional coaches support teams but do not manage them.

image.label: A small team meeting in a living room office
image.brief: 거실처럼 꾸민 작은 사무실에서 회의하는 팀.

slides.label: nurses and carers at Buurtzorg by the late 2010s, according to the company
body: And all of it was run with a very small head office for an organization of that size.

image.label: Many small team icons across a map
image.brief: 지도 위에 퍼진 작은 팀 아이콘들.

head: Fewer hours,
better care.
body: Consulting studies reported that Buurtzorg clients needed fewer hours of care than average, partly because nurses helped them become more independent.
Buurtzorg was also named the best employer in the Netherlands several times.

image.label: An elderly man walking again with a cane

head: Not a model you
can simply copy.
body: Self-management takes training, trust and simple shared tools. Organizations that copied the structure without those often struggled.

image.label: A training workshop with sticky notes
image.brief: 포스트잇이 붙은 벽 앞의 교육 워크숍.

head: Give the work back to
the people doing it.
body: Nurses closest to each client made the decisions, so care fit the person. Autonomy and purpose kept staff engaged.
Decentralizing worked because teams were small, clearly accountable and supported by simple systems.

image.label: Hands passing a key to a team

head: Who should really
make this decision?
body: Often the best decisions are made by the people nearest the customer, if they have the tools and trust to make them.
**Try it today:** pick one approval in your business. Could the team doing the work decide it themselves?

image.label: A bicycle parked by a front door

factChecks.note: Jos de Blok의 2006년 설립과 첫 팀 지역(엔스헤데 일대로 알려짐)은 Buurtzorg 공식 자료로 확인하세요. 카드에는 지역명을 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2006년 설립 확인(첫 팀 운영은 2007년으로 적은 자료도 있음).
팀당 최대 12명, 지역 코치 체계, 작은 백오피스는 회사 설명과 Laloux(2014)에 근거합니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 팀당 최대 12명, 코치 지원 확인.
"2010년대 후반 1만 명 이상" 인력 규모는 회사 발표 기준입니다. 시점별 수치가 달라 "by the late 2010s"로 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2014년 무렵 1만 명 이상 확인(최근 약 1만 5천 명).
돌봄 시간이 평균보다 적다는 결과는 Ernst & Young(2009), KPMG(2015) 보고서 기준이며 연구마다 결론과 수치가 다릅니다. 카드에는 수치를 넣지 않았습니다.
"네덜란드 최고 직장" 수상(2011년부터 여러 차례)은 수상 기관 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 네덜란드 최고 직장 여러 차례 선정 확인(횟수는 자료마다 다름).

sources.text: KPMG (2015). The added value of Buurtzorg versus other providers of home care.
Laloux, F. (2014). Reinventing Organizations. Nelson Parker.
